findings.text: blocking: _stop_delivered_reviews pre-writes its attribution record with _write_sender_record(_run_directory(pointer), target_pid=int(pid), reason="delivered-review-outlived-grace") and then calls signal_run(int(pid), pointer.get("pid_start_time")) at line 867, where signal_run defaults to _signal_process_group at line 847; it passes neither run_dir nor reason, so the guard's refused outcome is written nowhere on this production path (reached from watch_follow -> watch_ticker -> _stop_delivered_reviews at recovery.py:8632), leaving the run's sender file with an outcome-less attribution line — the defect the node's explicit goal ("every production caller ... passes the directory") exists to remove. recovery.py is in this node's declared write scope, and the receipt's "all seven call sites" undercounts to eight because this call goes through the signal_run alias rather than the literal _signal_process_group the receipt greps; the two-argument Callable[[int, str | None], None] signature cannot carry run_dir, so wiring it needs that signature widened or the call inlined.

follow-on: the unwatch caller also passes neither run_dir nor reason, so on a guard refusal its attribution record into the shared watch senders.jsonl has no outcome either; the node discloses this and the blocker is a genuine out-of-scope assertion (tests/test_unwatch_leaves_a_sender_record.py asserts len(records) == 1, which a second outcome line would break), so the repair needs a scope extension over that test or a change teaching signal_worker not to duplicate a caller's pre-written attribution, not a reimplementation here.

item_verdicts.diff: read 8753de02f against base 1880dac7; dispatch.py +21/-3 (three callers gain run_dir+reason), promotion.py +14/-2 (settle and release), recovery.py +14/-2 (budget-watchdog gains run_dir+reason; the unwatch pre-write gains detail=), plus a 147-line test and a 26-line evidence fragment; routing.py is untouched, so the guard itself is byte-identical to base and only the call sites moved.
item_verdicts.done_when: the node's own measure (six callers wired, one guard test per module, a logged negative control, zero added failures across four named files) is met as stated: gate 3 passed EXIT=0, base and head arms 17 passed / 17 passed, negative control 17 failed case red EXIT=1. Measured against the explicit goal of every production caller, the done-when's own test covers only 3 of the 6 wired callers and none of the 2 unwired ones, so it cannot falsify the remaining calls.
item_verdicts.goal: the goal is that every production caller of _signal_process_group passes the directory its sender record was written to. Six run-bearing callers now do (dispatch.py:6222/9900/10031, promotion.py:3795/5583, recovery.py:3045), so a guard refusal lands in the run's own senders.jsonl; the mechanism is proven by the new gate and its negative control. Two production callers still pass neither run_dir nor reason: the unwatch caller at recovery.py:7434 (disclosed) and _stop_delivered_reviews at recovery.py:867 (undisclosed), the latter reached through the signal_run alias rather than the literal function name.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; status complete, carrying machine-readable baseline_suite (1880dac7, completed true, failure_count 0) and after_suite (8753de02f, completed true, failure_count 0), the negative-control log, measurement_module/measurement_cwd, and a follow_on that discloses the unwatch caller; it does NOT disclose _stop_delivered_reviews, and its receipt claims all seven call sites of the guard (there are eight).
item_verdicts.write_paths: the declared paths are dispatch.py, promotion.py, recovery.py, the gate test and an evidence fragment; git show --stat 8753de02f touches exactly those five and nothing else, and recovery.py (where the miss sits) is in scope.

justifications.durability: the added assertion is genuinely falsifiable — dropping run_dir from the promotion caller leaves the run's sender file with only its attribution line and no refused outcome, reddening test_promotion_settle (negative-control.log, 1 failed 2 passed EXIT=1); however the suite stays green with _stop_delivered_reviews still unwired because no test drives it, so a regression on that production path is uncatchable by the current gate.
justifications.evidence: the done-when's artefacts reproduce independently at head 8753de02f (named gate 3 passed EXIT=0, review-gate.log), the base log names 1880dac7 with 17 passed and the head arm log names 8753de02f with 17 passed (zero added failures), and the negative control reddens the promotion case EXIT=1; but the gate drives only dispatch.terminate, promotion-settle and recovery budget-watchdog, so 3 of the 6 wired callers and both unwired ones are unmeasured, and tests/test_a_delivered_review_ends_its_turn.py substitutes a fake signal_run, so no test exercises the real delivered-review refusal path.
justifications.fit: the changes reuse the existing _write_sender_record run_dir/reason/detail keyword surface in reckon/crew/routing.py:1530 without widening it, match the surrounding pre-write-then-signal idiom, add no plan/sprint/ticket identifier to any name or comment, and the new test follows the repo's synthetic-RECKON_HOME fixture convention.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the goal names EVERY production caller, and eight exist; six now pass run_dir (dispatch.py:6222/9900/10031, promotion.py:3795/5583, recovery.py:3045) but recovery.py:867 (_stop_delivered_reviews, via the signal_run alias at recovery.py:847) and recovery.py:7434 (unwatch) still pass neither run_dir nor reason, so a guard refusal on those paths writes no outcome record — the exact defect the node exists to remove — and the missed caller is inside the node's own declared write scope (recovery.py).
justifications.scope_discipline: git show --stat 8753de02f changes exactly the five declared paths and no others; the unwatch caller's run_dir is left unwired rather than worked around the fence, and the deviation is disclosed in follow_ons with its out-of-scope test collision named; the miss at recovery.py:867 is a completeness gap inside an in-scope file, not a scope violation.
